analysis: This is one of the bigger model-vs-market disagreements on direction this week, not just magnitude. Elo has Pittsburgh, at home, favored by 2.8 points, and the team's actual scoring margin over its last logged games backs that up almost exactly (+0.1) -- two independent signals agreeing the home team is the better side right now. The market disagrees: both DraftKings and Caesars have Cincinnati favored on the road, -3.5. Neither roster carries a real injury story into this one; an early report crediting a Colts receiver to the Steelers was a clean misattribution and nothing else moved either projection.

That's a 6.3-point gap between what the model thinks and what the market is charging -- Pittsburgh, as a home team the model actually likes, is getting +3.5 points in a game where the market has them as the road-favored underdog on paper. 66.7% of sim runs have the Steelers covering that number, which lines up with the model's own read: it isn't saying Cincinnati loses, just that +3.5 is a lot of points to hand a team Elo has as the better side at home.

leans.reasoning: Model favors the home team (Steelers +2.8) while the market favors the road team (Bengals -3.5) -- a real 6.3-pt directional disagreement, and 66.7% of sims have Pittsburgh covering the current number.
